meta.title: Bruno Pizza — Product case study | Julien Esterbet

hero.title: Bruno Pizza — Production
hero.subtitle: A local desktop application that turns an Excel plan into an actionable workshop production flow.
hero.imageAlt: Bruno Pizza production dashboard showing quantities by variety and distributor

overview.status: Active product · v1.2.0 in acceptance testing

problem.title: From production file to workshop use
problem.body: The need is concrete: distribute pizza production across several distributors, validate imported quantities and then guide preparation variety by variety. A spreadsheet provides the data, but it is not an interface designed for the production workflow.

solution.title: A guided local business workflow
solution.intro: Version 1.2 brings the Excel plan closer to workshop practice: adjust quantities, recover imported values and follow assembly steps in pictures.

dashboard.title: Production dashboard
dashboard.body: Excel import excludes Kit Pizza rows and groups quantities by pizza and location. Quantities can be adjusted with recalculated totals. Changes are highlighted in yellow, saved locally and can be reset to the imported values after confirmation.

workshop.title: Workshop flow
workshop.body: Ordered recipes and an assembly gallery: photos play at an adjustable pace, with pause, navigation and access to the final image. Zero-quantity pizzas are skipped; the next pizza stays visible to help prepare ahead.

settings.title: Business settings
settings.body: Local management of the catalogue, recipes and locations. Up to 20 photos per pizza can be added, reordered or removed with confirmation; the last one represents the finished result.

architecture.title: A full-stack chain packaged with Electron

steps.excel: The Excel file remains the source of the production plan.
steps.react: React and TypeScript power the interface and presentation rules.
steps.express: Express exposes a strictly local API bound to 127.0.0.1.
steps.sqlite: SQLite stores the business catalogue and recipes on the machine.
steps.electron: Electron starts the backend on an available port and provides the desktop application.

decisions.title: Make local use reliable before expanding the scope

local.title: Local operation
local.body: Data, pictures and settings remain on the machine. The server is not designed to be exposed directly to the Internet.

persistence.title: Separated persistence
persistence.body: The catalogue and photos remain outside the installation files. Gallery migration preserves existing images and backs up the existing database; plan adjustments are saved separately in local storage.

quality.title: Verifiable delivery
quality.body: As of 2 October 2026, the v1.2.0 release log reports 67 automated tests, a packaged macOS build and an in-app check. Windows acceptance testing remains pending. Version 1.1.4 had been validated in the workshop on a 43-inch screen.

items.excel: Excel remains the initial source of the plan, with traceable local adjustments; Adial integration is not included.
items.trust: The application targets trusted local use and does not include the authentication required for network exposure.
items.signing: The Windows and macOS test releases are not signed yet.
items.validation: Version 1.2.0 is an acceptance-test build: Windows packaging and workshop feedback are still pending.

next.title: An application designed for the workshop
next.body: The public repository documents the complete flow, from Excel plan import to local persistence and desktop packaging.

release.title: Adjust, illustrate, prepare
release.body: This iteration addresses three practical needs: adjust a plan without losing the Excel reference, make assembly steps visible and improve readability during production. The dark theme is now permanent and images stay uncropped.

meta.title: My-Website — Portfolio case study | Julien Esterbet

hero.title: My-Website
hero.subtitle: A bilingual, interactive portfolio bringing together my projects, experiments and more personal work.
hero.imageAlt: My-Website homepage presenting Julien Esterbet and his full-stack positioning

problem.title: Present my work without reducing myself to a list of technologies
problem.body: My-Website is both my professional portfolio and a space for exploration. It presents products I have actually built, makes my technical decisions visible and also opens onto Web3, travel and writing. A recruiter can understand my profile quickly, while curious visitors can explore the site at several levels.

solution.title: A professional showcase that remains personal
solution.intro: The site organizes content into distinct worlds and gives each one the right format: product case study, interactive prototype, travel journal or reflection.

architecture.title: Navigation by world
architecture.body: Portfolio, Web3, travel and reflections each have their own page, local navigation and bilingual content while sharing a coherent visual identity.

media.title: Images for every screen
media.body: Portraits, screenshots and albums are served in several sizes and modern formats to preserve quality without sending original files to visitors.

quality.title: Useful interactions
quality.body: The map, globe, galleries, timelines, Web3 tools and language switch enrich the visit while preserving keyboard paths and readable alternatives.

steps.entry: Vite initializes React, internationalization and performance measurements.
steps.shell: AppShell owns the skip link, navigation, main content, loading states and global error handling.
steps.routes: Each page and its translation namespace are loaded on demand from a single route registry.
steps.domains: Home, Web3, Travel and Reflections remain organized by domain; external calls go through dedicated services.
steps.media: ResponsiveImage consumes generated manifests to select the appropriate format and width for each context.
steps.vercel: The static build targets Vercel with Node 24, reproducible installs, a real 404 and long-lived caching limited to versioned assets.

incremental.title: Continuous evolution
incremental.body: The site is a living product: projects, trips and articles can grow without requiring the entire architecture to be rebuilt.

privacy.title: Separate sources and derivatives
privacy.body: Originals remain working sources; only cleaned and optimized variants are intended for the public site.

accessibility.title: Audit before declaration
accessibility.body: RGAA work uses a criterion matrix and manual evidence. Local results do not become a compliance statement before the deployed version is checked again.

adapters.title: Isolate external dependencies
adapters.body: Email, Mapbox, RPC, price data and wallet inspection go through adapters that separate the interface from providers.

challenges.title: Bring several experiences together in one site

legacy.title: Preserve consistency
legacy.body: Very different albums, articles, tools and case studies must remain identifiable without fragmenting the overall experience.

interactive.title: Make interaction accessible
interactive.body: The globe, map, timeline, carousels, dialogs and Web3 tools require text alternatives, keyboard navigation and careful focus management.

editorial.title: Remain credible
editorial.body: Active, academic and historical projects must be named by their real status, with results limited to what the code or audits can prove.

items.delivery: Read case studies explaining the need, behaviour, architecture and trade-offs behind each project.
items.performance: Explore Web3 prototypes, inspect public addresses and understand the technical areas that interest me.
items.media: Navigate my trips through a globe, a map, a timeline and responsive photo galleries.
items.rgaa: Read longer reflections in a bilingual interface designed for keyboard navigation and small screens.

items.deployment: React and React Router structure a single-page application split into routes loaded on demand.
items.mediaDelivery: Vite produces the static build deployed on Vercel, with SEO pages generated for the main routes.
items.securityHeaders: Mapbox, blockchain RPC, price and email calls go through dedicated services rather than interface components.
items.cv: i18next powers the French and English versions, while travel and project content lives in structured data.
items.font: Vitest, Testing Library, axe-core, ESLint and TypeScript protect important behaviour before builds.
items.fieldData: Responsive media, build budgets and lazy loading control the cost of the richest pages.

next.body: The public repository exposes the architecture, data, tests and delivery choices behind the visible experience.

hero.title: OpenDente. Charging at your pace.
hero.subtitle: My edition of a native utility that adapts Mac charging to your day. Simple profiles, clear battery information and your settings, right in the menu bar.
hero.lightAlt: OpenDente in English: charging panel in light appearance
hero.darkAlt: OpenDente in English: dark panel with Desk, Daily and Travel profiles
hero.caption: Real screenshots · Light and dark appearance

overview.status: Personal Edition 0.8.0 · Public source, built and signed locally.
overview.role: Extending an open source project: new workflows, bilingual interface and experimental native control.
overview.scope: macOS 14+ · Hardware checks on a MacBook Air M3 running macOS 27.2.

intent.title: A quiet tool for an everyday need.
intent.body: A Mac is used differently at a desk, on the move or before a long period in storage. I extended OpenDente to make these situations easier to manage: keep everyday charging preferences, read the actual battery state and enable a temporary mode without losing those settings.

daily.title: Settings that follow your day
daily.body: Desk, Daily and Travel profiles, a one-off full charge and storage preparation at 50%: temporary modes preserve the everyday configuration.

interface.title: An interface that belongs on Mac
interface.body: French and English, light and dark appearance, percentage inside the battery icon and customizable measurements keep the essentials easy to read.

background.title: There when it is needed
background.body: Quiet login startup, configurable MagSafe signals, an offline guide and optional local diagnostics. No account or telemetry server added.

gallery.title: A small panel. Thoughtful controls.
gallery.note: Real screenshots from version 0.8.0. Customizable thresholds shown as examples.

charge.label: Charging settings
charge.title: A ceiling and a resume threshold.
charge.body: Choose a daily limit, decide when charging resumes and find the options in one place. An additional thermal pause can be configured; macOS protections retain priority.
charge.alt: OpenDente charging settings in English: 80% limit, return to the ceiling and resume below 70%

profiles.label: Everyday profiles
profiles.title: From your desk to your next trip.
profiles.body: The panel brings together profiles, storage preparation and a one-off charge to 100%. The percentage, active mode and energy flows help explain what is happening.
profiles.alt: OpenDente panel in English, dark appearance: everyday profiles, storage at 50% and one-off full charge

menu.label: Menu bar
menu.title: The essentials, without a window.
menu.body: The percentage sits inside the battery. Temperature, power and charging mode can complete the display, with a choice of compact or classic layout.
menu.alt: OpenDente menu bar settings in English: compact display and optional indicators

magsafe.label: MagSafe signals
magsafe.title: Status at the end of the cable.
magsafe.body: Assign a fixed color, slow blink or alternating pattern to each charging state. A ten-second preview makes each signal easy to check.
magsafe.alt: OpenDente MagSafe settings in English: colors, blinking patterns and signal previews

guide.label: Built-in guide
guide.title: Understand a setting as you use it.
guide.body: An offline guide explains profiles, thresholds, temporary modes and their limits. Search helps find an answer without leaving the application.
guide.alt: OpenDente built-in guide in English with search and explanations of profiles and temporary modes

engineering.title: A native experience, from panel to system.
engineering.body: The SwiftUI interface stays separate from privileged operations. This edition adds an experimental native mechanism, settings restoration and recovery checks while preserving the original project’s architecture and history.

steps.app: The SwiftUI application reads measurements and applies the user’s profiles and preferences.
steps.helper: A certificate-authenticated XPC connection delegates privileged operations to the local helper.
steps.system: The helper uses the available SMC or native mechanism. A recovery journal and watchdog support settings restoration.

context.title: Real checks, with compatibility still to expand.
context.body: Native control uses private Apple interfaces and remains experimental. Documented hardware checks cover a MacBook Air M3; they do not validate every Mac. A request can take several minutes and is not an immediate hardware cutoff. The application is built and signed locally; no notarized public installer is provided.

credits.title: Built on an open project
credits.before: This edition is a fork of
credits.after: . The original charging features and architecture come from that project; my additions extend this foundation and preserve its credits and history.
credits.license: GPL-3.0 source code. Other contributions and their licenses are detailed in the repository.
